All 5 generateContent calls now send store=false via a shared config (src/lib/geminiStore.js) using httpOptions.extraBody, since SDK 1.7.0 has no typed `store`. No SDK bump. Added scripts/check-store.mjs, which runs the real SDK with a mocked fetch and asserts the body contains store:false.

- `scripts/check-store.mjs`
- `src/components/ChatPanel.jsx`
- `src/components/CodeConverter.jsx`
- `src/components/CodeDebugger.jsx`
- `src/components/LeftPanel.jsx`
- `src/components/RightPanel.jsx`
- `src/lib/geminiStore.js`

### Why

Changelog: new paid-tier projects "now store requests by default (store=true)". This app sends user source code, so we opt out explicitly.

> now store requests by default
> (`store=true`), matching the Interactions API.

Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/changelog.md.txt

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| build | pass | pass | 0 |
| store-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

Provider validators: none run.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Whether the API accepts a top-level `store` in the generateContent body (no live call).
- Whether the project's key is on a new paid-tier project.
- Account-level opt-out in Logs and Datasets settings is an alternative that code can't verify.
- Users' own keys on other tiers: store:false is sent regardless.
- No provider validator was run.

- extraBody is untyped; if the API rejected `store`, calls would error rather than silently fall back.

review.summary: The diff adds `config: GEMINI_NO_STORE_CONFIG` to all five named generateContent calls (ChatPanel ~L108, CodeConverter ~L132, CodeDebugger ~L128, LeftPanel ~L158, RightPanel ~L148). If the API returns 400 for an unknown or unsupported field, all five Gemini paths fail. Check the quoted changelog and the Generate Content REST reference for the exact field name and placement.

It does not exercise a real response, so it does not justify 'verified' for runtime behaviour.

This is a behavioural and policy decision, not a forced migration: the app now explicitly opts every user out of storage. That is reasonable for a client-side app that uses user-supplied keys, but a human should confirm it is intended. Features that depend on stored requests, such as Interactions-style retrieval, would not work.
